summary: Tan Poh Beng specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Charles Willemen and Tilak Kariyawasam, and also studied under Gallelle Sumanasiri and Shengshou.
Tan Sitong was an 1865–1898 scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied under Wang Zhengyi and later under Yang Wenhui from circa 1895 to 1898.

Tan Yun-shan (1898–1983) worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. After studying at institutions including Hunan First Normal University and Chuanshan Academy, he taught at Lida Academy (~1924–1926) and served as Professor of Chinese Studies at Visva-Bharati University (~1937–1966).

Tanaya Afroz is a linguist who conducted doctoral research under Shyam Sundar Bhattacharya (attested 2026). She held an appointment as a Research Scholar/Fellow at The Asiatic Society, attested in 2026.

Tanero Sasakawa (1870–1949) was a scholar of Sinology, history and archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1893–1896) and later held positions at Toyo University and Meiji University (~1920–1944).

Tang Yijie (1927–2014) was a scholar of philosophy and Sinology who studied at Peking University (~1947–1951). He served as a professor at Peking University (~1956–2014) and held a post at Stanford University (~1989–1991).

Tania Singer studied at the University of Marburg (~1989–1992), Technical University of Berlin (~1992–1996), and Free University of Berlin (~1996–2000). She held academic posts at the University of Zurich (~2006–2010) and the University of Leipzig (~2010–2018).

Tansen Sen works in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University and earned a PhD from the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair, later holding a post at Baruch College attested in 2003.
Tanso Hirose (1782–1856) was a scholar of Sinology, philosophy, and Japanology. He studied under Hōdō and at Kamei Juku (~1797–1801), and founded Kangien in 1801.

Tanzan Hara (1819–1892) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy educated at Yushima Seido and Shoheizaka Gakumonjo. He served at the Ministry of Religion (1872–1874), University of Tokyo (1879), and as superintendent at Komazawa University (1891).

Tao Jiang is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at Temple University under Shigenori Nagatomo. In 2011, he was attested as an Associate Professor in the Department of Religion at Rutgers University.
Tao Jin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed a PhD at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 2008 under the supervision of Alexander Leonhard Mayer.
Tao Pan works in the fields of Indology and linguistics. He completed a BA at Fudan University in 2010 and earned a Magister Artium from the University of Munich.

Tara Doyle is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She has held posts at Emory University, including lecturer and director of its Tibetan Studies Program (attested 2003) and Professor Emerita (attested 2026).

Tarab Tulku XI (1934–2004) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as a curator at the Royal Danish Library (~1962–1999) and held a post at the University of Copenhagen (~1968–1998).

Tarthang Tulku is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology educated at Tarthang Monastery and under various traditional teachers. He held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1962–1968), Tibetan Nyingma Meditation Center (~1969), and Nyingma Institute (~1972).

Tashi Rabgey is a Tibetologist who studied at University College, Toronto, Magdalen College, the University of Cambridge, and Harvard University. She served as a lecturer and Tibet Center co-director at the University of Virginia (~2008–2011) and joined Georgetown University (~2011).

Tashi Samphel is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He has served as director of the Songtsen Library (attested 2015) and as an Associate Professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2026).

Tashi Tsering is a scholar of Tibetology, history, archaeology, and linguistics who studied at the Central School for Tibetans, Dalhousie. He served at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (~1979–1992) and Amnye Machen Institute (~1992).

Tatiana Oranskaia works in Indology and linguistics. After studying at Saint Petersburg State University and the Central Institute of Hindi, she held posts at Saint Petersburg State University (1973–1998) and the University of Hamburg (1995–1996; 1998–2016).
